A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same oracle-complexity research, with corresponding main sections and complete Appendices A and B. Text, equations, and page renderings support comparison; neither version contains figures or tables.

before.justification: V1 presents mathematical constructions, lower bounds, and proofs, including its appendices. It reports no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: V3 remains entirely theoretical. Its added appendix material consists of mathematical arguments, not original empirical results.

M1.justification: The central hard-instance construction for q > p+ν changes from Gaussian smoothing truncated to an ℓ2 ball to truncation within an ℓ∞ ball (Definition 4). The oracle-indistinguishability construction consequently uses ℓ∞ neighborhoods. This changes the procedure's sampling support and locality, rather than merely its description.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical training/evaluation tasks. Optimization examples in the introduction remain motivational examples.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. Comparisons with previously published complexity bounds are theoretical research positioning.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an empirical evaluation protocol, data splits, training budgets, or testing procedures. Changes to oracle assumptions and analytical parameters concern the theory.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, empirical robustness tests, error analyses, or case studies. The supplementary material provides proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetitions, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Probability calculations within the smoothing proofs are theoretical, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: There are no empirical result entries in either version. Changes to complexity expressions and smoothness constants are analytical results assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V3 revises the truncation definition and locality proof, adds the normalization/marginal-distribution Lemma 13 and a proof of Lemma 2, and replaces the central smoothness argument in Appendix A.1. The smoothness constant changes from 6/(5ρ) to 2/ρ, with corresponding downstream adjustments. Theorem 2 also gains explicit accuracy dependence and both theorems specify deterministic algorithms.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace the ε-independent expression printed with log² for q < p+ν with an explicit log log expression containing 1/ε. The conclusion also restricts the second construction to deterministic/zero-respecting algorithms. These materially revise the stated rate and applicability while retaining the overarching matching-lower-bounds contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 newly explains why the original ℓ2-ball marginal argument introduces dimension dependence and motivates hypercube truncation. Section 6 distinguishes the first construction's claimed randomized extension from the second construction's deterministic limitation. The bounded-domain caveat and omission of q = p+ν were already present.

D1.justification: No implementation, hardware, runtime, or code/data-access information is added or removed. The revised construction parameters are analytical proof choices.

R1.justification: V3 adds Cartinhour, Birnbaum and Andrews, Chen et al., Carmon et al. (2020), and Roulet and d’Aspremont, while removing Bensimhoun. These support the revised distribution arguments and applicability discussion; the broader positioning against existing oracle-complexity bounds remains.

P1.justification: The six main sections and Appendices A–B retain their organization. Local explanatory passages, terminology, cross-references, and author-name text change; the auxiliary H(x) is renamed R(x). Most existing prose and the second construction's exposition remain.

P2.justification: V3 adopts the ICLR conference template, changing the title treatment, running headers, heading typography, equation spacing, and page breaks. Both retain a single-column layout without figures or tables.

improvement.justification: V3 clarifies accuracy dependence and deterministic scope, and repairs v1's marginal-distribution assumption through cube truncation. However, the replacement smoothness proof in Appendix A.1 assumes a Euclidean-distance ordering that cube-truncated densities do not preserve and uses asymptotic normal convergence as an exact density calculation. These gaps leave the central dimension-free guarantee unsupported by the presented argument, so the net quality improvement is uncertain.
